c1.body: The caterer wants to know how many children's meals to prepare. Guests who reply through their personal link report separately how many adults and how many children are coming, and the breakdown appears next to their name on the list. A reply in a WhatsApp message is recorded as one total.
c1.title: Children and adults are counted separately

c2.body: A classmate won't answer messages, but their parent will. The invitation goes to the parent's number, and the reply is recorded under the child's name.
c2.title: Parents reply for their children

c3.body: You can import the contacts from the class group instead of typing in thirty names and numbers by hand.
c3.title: The class list comes as a WhatsApp list

c4.body: Family replies fast, colleagues reply late and the class hardly replies at all. Filtering the list by group and status shows exactly where the replies are stuck.

challenges.eyebrow: Why a bar mitzvah is different

q1.answer: The form that opens from the personal link has one field for adults and another for children, and the numbers appear next to the guest's name on the list. Guests who reply directly in the WhatsApp message report one total, with no breakdown.
q1.question: How do you count children and adults separately?

q2.answer: The invitation goes to the parent's number, and the automatic reminders continue only to those who haven't replied yet. Filtering the list to the class group and the "Pending" status shows exactly which classmates haven't replied yet.
q2.question: What do you do when your child's friend doesn't reply?

q3.answer: Yes. A bar mitzvah and a bat mitzvah are managed in exactly the same way, with the same list, the same groups and the same reply tracking. You fill in the event name and the celebrant's details when you create the event.
q3.question: Can I manage a bat mitzvah on the same system?

g1.body: Most celebrations have three circles: family, classmates and the parents' colleagues. When you put each circle in its own group, you can filter the list by group and status and see early on which circle hasn't replied yet.
g1.heading: Three circles, three reply speeds

g2.body: You invite classmates through a parent's phone, and the name on the list is the child's. The parent gets the message, replies on the child's behalf and also reports whether a sibling or parent is coming along.
g2.heading: A classmate's invitation goes to the parent

g3.body: When the aliyah to the Torah and the party take place on different days with different guests, each one is a separate event on KALFA, with its own list and replies. That way, someone invited only to the synagogue isn't counted at the party by mistake.
g3.heading: Aliyah and party: two events, two lists

guide.title: The guide to bar and bat mitzvah RSVPs

hero.lede: Three different lists at one event: family, classmates and the parents' colleagues. Each one acts differently, and they all have to add up to one number.

timing.t1: Collect the class list from parents or from the WhatsApp group about a month before. This is the part that takes the longest.
timing.t2: Divide guests into groups (family, class, work) and import them into KALFA before the RSVP round starts.
timing.t3: Keep an eye on the class group. It's usually the last to reply, so that's where to check who's still missing.
timing.t4: Give the caterer your numbers after the last message in the round, with a breakdown of adults and children.

c1.body: There are usually just two or three days between the announcement and the event. There's no time to build a list from scratch, so importing an existing list makes all the difference.
c1.title: You have days, not weeks

c2.body: These days are taken up with entirely different things. Once the invitations are sent, reminders and tracking keep running without anyone having to sit over them.
c2.title: Parents have no time to manage a list

c3.body: Replies keep coming in even on the morning of the event. A live overview beats a list printed yesterday.
c3.title: The numbers keep moving until the last moment

c4.body: Everyone on the list is contacted automatically, instead of you copying the same text into dozens of separate chats.
c4.title: You need to reach everyone fast

q1.answer: Setting up the event takes minutes, and importing an existing list from a file or from WhatsApp saves you the typing. You can activate RSVPs on the same day the date is set.
q1.question: How long does it take to set up an event and send invitations?

q2.answer: Yes. Once RSVPs are activated, guests are contacted at the points still left in the sending schedule before the event, and not on Shabbat, on Jewish holidays or at night. Anything scheduled for a point that has already passed isn't sent late.
q2.question: Can I activate RSVPs for a brit milah just a few days before?

q3.answer: Yes. A britah, a zeved habat and a brit milah are all managed the same way: an event, a guest list and reply tracking. The only difference is usually that you have more time to prepare.
q3.question: Does the same work for a britah?

g1.body: A brit milah takes place on the eighth day of the baby's life, so only a few days pass between the moment the date is known and the event itself. That makes speed of setup the most important thing: importing an existing list from a file or from WhatsApp saves you the typing, and your event is ready in minutes.
g1.heading: Why a brit milah comes together in days, not weeks

g2.body: For a britah or zeved habat, ceremonies that welcome a baby girl, the date is more flexible, but the list is similar: close family, friends and people who live nearby. The same process works here too: create an event, import the list and activate RSVPs.
g2.heading: Also for a britah or zeved habat

g3.body: Messages aren't sent on Shabbat, on Jewish holidays or at night. A message due at one of those times is automatically rescheduled to the next sending window, so no guest receives a message on Shabbat.
g3.heading: When the brit milah falls close to Shabbat or a Jewish holiday

c1.body: A venue or room has a fixed number of places. Keeping track of how many have confirmed stops you from finding out too late that too many have signed up.
c1.title: A capacity you can't exceed

c2.body: On an entry list, "roughly" doesn't work. The updated list is available at any moment, with no need to export a version that's out of date right away.
c2.title: An accurate entry list

c3.body: Dividing guests into groups lets you filter the list by department or guest type and see exactly who in each group hasn't replied yet.

c4.body: A clear summary of the numbers for whoever orders the food, manages the entrance or needs to pass them on.

q1.answer: Yes. Each guest can belong to a group, such as a department, a guest type or any other division, and you can filter the guest list by group and reply status.
q1.question: Can I divide guests into groups?

q2.answer: Each guest reports how many people their invitation covers, and the number updates in real time. Those who haven't replied yet and those who answered "Maybe" are shown separately, so it's clear how much of the number is still uncertain.
q2.question: How do I know how many people will really come?

q3.answer: If a number was set for the invitation, the RSVP form won't let them go over it. A WhatsApp reply with a higher number is saved and flagged for the host, who decides what to do.
q3.question: What happens if a guest tries to confirm more people than were invited?

g1.body: Set how many people each invitation covers. On the RSVP form, guests can't confirm more than that number, and a WhatsApp reply that goes over it is flagged for the host, so going over capacity shows up early and not at the door.
g1.heading: How to stay within capacity

g2.body: A guest can reply "Maybe", and that reply is kept separate from "Attending" and "Not attending". That way you can see how many places are still uncertain and don't count them as confirmed by mistake.
g2.heading: What to do with "Maybe"

g3.body: At a conference or company evening, guests come from departments, clients and partners. A group for each source lets you filter the list and see who from each one has confirmed, and a guest can add a note, for example the name of someone coming in their place.
g3.heading: Business events: who invited whom

c1.body: Each side manages its own guests, and mutual friends appear twice. Importing both lists into one place exposes the duplicates instead of hiding them.

c2.body: One invitation to a family could mean two people or six. When each guest reports how many are coming with them, the number stops being a guess.
c2.title: Not knowing how many plus-ones will come

c3.body: Some who confirm don't come, and some who stay silent do. Keeping track of who hasn't replied yet shrinks the group of unknowns before you lock in your numbers.
c3.title: The gap between "I'm coming" and who actually shows up

c4.body: Chasing 300 people by phone is a week's work. An automatic reminder goes only to those who haven't replied yet, and doesn't bother those who already have.

challenges.title: Four problems that come up at almost every wedding

q1.answer: The invitation or Save the Date goes out weeks ahead, but it's better to ask "who's coming?" close to the date, when the answers are accurate. On KALFA, the RSVP round and reminders go out automatically in the days before the wedding, and no messages are sent on Shabbat or Jewish holidays.
q1.question: When do you ask for wedding RSVPs?

q2.answer: You can import each list separately, from a file or from WhatsApp, and mark it as its own group. A phone number that's already on the list is flagged in the import draft with the existing guest's name, so you can decide before sending and avoid sending to the same person twice.
q2.question: How do you merge both sides' guest lists?

q3.answer: Yes. Each guest gets their own private link and sees only their own details, not the guest list and not anyone else's replies.
q3.question: Does every guest get a personal link?

q4.answer: No. The message arrives on WhatsApp, and guests reply with a tap or through their personal link, which opens in the phone's browser. There's nothing to sign up for or install.
q4.question: Do guests need to install an app?

q5.answer: The full details, including the packages, the price of each and what's included, are on the FAQ page, which updates directly from the packages in the system.
q5.question: How much does it cost to manage wedding RSVPs?

g1.body: An RSVP is each guest's reply: whether they're coming and how many people are coming with them. The replies add up to the number you give the venue and the caterer, so it's worth collecting them in one place rather than in dozens of separate calls. On KALFA, a guest can reply with a tap in the WhatsApp message, or through a personal link where they choose Attending, Maybe or Not attending, report how many adults and children are coming and add a note if they want to.
g1.heading: What a wedding RSVP is

g2.body: The printed invitation and the Save the Date announce the date, so they go out weeks ahead. The RSVP asks who's really coming, so it works best close to the date, when guests already know their plans. On KALFA, the RSVP round goes out automatically in the days before the wedding, following the schedule further down this page.
g2.heading: Printed invitation, Save the Date and RSVP: three different things

g3.body: Import each side's list separately, from a CSV file (Excel saves in this format) or from WhatsApp, and assign each row to a group such as "Groom's side", "Bride's side" or "Friends". Before the import reaches your list you see a draft, and a phone number that already belongs to another guest is flagged there with that guest's name, so duplicates show up before sending, not after.
g3.heading: How to merge two sides' guest lists

g4.body: Guests who have replied get no more reminders. The automatic reminders continue only to those who haven't replied yet. The overview updates with every reply, so you can see at any moment how many have confirmed and how many are still pending, and you can filter the list by side or group to see who in it hasn't replied yet.
g4.heading: What happens with those who don't reply

googleSheets.answer: Yes. Upload the file to Google Sheets and share it, and when the list is ready, download it again as a CSV. That's the same format KALFA imports.
googleSheets.question: Can I work on the list in Google Sheets with my partner?

howToBuild.answer: Start with one file per side, one row per invitation with a quantity column, a group for each row and a mobile number in a single format. At the end, merge the files and check for duplicates by phone number, before anyone gets an invitation.
howToBuild.question: How do you build a wedding guest list?

importToKalfa.answer: Yes. It's exactly the same template as on KALFA's guest import screen, with the same columns. You can fill it in now and import it later without changing a thing.
importToKalfa.question: Can I import this file into KALFA?

listGrows.answer: A spreadsheet works great for building the list in the first place. It stops working when you need to send a personal invitation for every row, track who replied and remind only those who haven't replied yet. Updating hundreds of rows by hand is the main source of mistakes.
listGrows.question: What happens as the list grows?

opensInExcel.answer: Yes. The file is a UTF-8 CSV with a BOM, which is what makes Excel display Hebrew correctly. It also opens in Google Sheets and Numbers with no conversion.
opensInExcel.question: Does the template open in Excel?

rowPerInvite.answer: Because the invitation is the unit that gets sent. The Cohen family gets one invitation covering four people. The quantity column says how many, so the number of invitations and the number of guests stay two separate, clear numbers.
rowPerInvite.question: Why one row per invitation and not per person?

file.intro: Four columns, and one row per <invite>invitation</invite>, not per person.
file.sampleNote: The row with no phone number is there on purpose: you can still manage a guest who has no number. They just won't get an automatic message.
file.title: What's in the file

hero.subtitle: A ready-made file with the right columns that opens in Excel and Google Sheets. You can start filling it in right away, and if you later want to manage your event on KALFA, it's the same template the system imports.

meta.description: A ready-made guest list template for a wedding or any event. Opens in Excel and Google Sheets, with name, phone, quantity and group columns. Free to download.

excelPhone.body: The leading zero disappears and 0501234567 becomes 501234567. Setting the column to text before you paste solves this.
excelPhone.title: Excel turns a phone number into a plain number

mixedPhones.body: 050-1234567, +972501234567 and 0501234567 are the same number in three forms. A consistent column saves you duplicates that only show up after sending.
mixedPhones.title: Phone numbers in mixed formats

noGroup.body: Without groups you can't tell which part of the list is falling behind on replies, and you can't focus your effort on just the part that hasn't replied yet.
noGroup.title: No group column

rowPerPerson.body: One family is one invitation with a quantity, not four separate rows. Splitting it into people inflates the list and makes it harder to count how many invitations were really sent.
rowPerPerson.title: A row per person instead of per invitation

mistakes.title: Four mistakes that show up in almost every spreadsheet guest list

groupPerRow.body: Groom's side, bride's side, work, friends: one group per row. Later, this is what lets you see which part of the list hasn't replied yet.
groupPerRow.title: A group for each row

mergeDedupe.body: When you import the files into KALFA, a phone number that's already on the list is flagged in the import draft with the existing guest's name, so a mutual friend doesn't get two invitations.
mergeDedupe.title: Merge and check for duplicates

ownCopy.body: When each family works on a separate file from the same template, nobody overwrites anyone else's changes. You merge once, at the end.
ownCopy.title: Each side fills in its own copy

phoneFormat.body: The phone column is set as text and holds one mobile number per row. Without a number you can still manage the guest, but they won't get an automatic invitation.
phoneFormat.title: Mobile numbers in one format

rowPerInvite.body: A couple is one row with a quantity of 2, and a family with children is one row with its own quantity. That way the number of invitations and the number of guests stay two separate numbers.
rowPerInvite.title: One row per invitation, with a quantity

anyText.answer: No. WhatsApp approves the structure of business-initiated messages in advance, and KALFA sends only approved templates. The personal details (name, date and place) change in each message.
anyText.question: Can I send any text I want?

guestsSeeEachOther.answer: No. Each message is sent separately, and each guest sees only their own details, not the guest list and not anyone else's replies.
guestsSeeEachOther.question: Can guests see each other?

howToSend.answer: Import your guest list, and KALFA sends a personal message to each number through WhatsApp's official business platform. There's no need to send from your own phone or open a group.
howToSend.question: How do you collect RSVPs on WhatsApp?

noWhatsapp.answer: They just won't receive anything on this channel. Their personal link still works by any other route, and you can also manage a guest with no phone number at all.
noWhatsapp.question: What happens if a guest doesn't have WhatsApp?

faq.moreLink: Pricing and the other channels are covered <faq>on the FAQ page</faq>.
faq.title: Sending on WhatsApp: common questions

hero.subtitle: A personal invitation for every guest through WhatsApp's official business platform. No group, no broadcast list, no sending by hand from your own phone.
hero.title: RSVPs on WhatsApp

items.approvedTemplate: A business-initiated message must use a template approved in advance by WhatsApp.
items.eventOnly: Messages are about the specific event and guest, not bulk advertising.
items.noGuarantee: Delivery depends on WhatsApp itself, so it isn't guaranteed for every number.
items.stopRequest: A guest who asks to stop receiving messages stops receiving them.

limits.title: WhatsApp is a platform with rules, and we follow them

meta.description: Send RSVP invitations and reminders on WhatsApp via the official platform: a personal message for every guest, a tap to reply and automatic tracking of replies.
meta.title: RSVPs on WhatsApp

autoRecorded.body: The guest replies from the message or from their personal link, and the status updates on the list without anyone typing it in.
autoRecorded.title: Replies record themselves

personal.body: Each guest gets their own message with their own details. There's no group, no broadcast list that everyone can see, and nobody is exposed to the guest list.
personal.title: A personal message, not a group message

reach.body: Guests don't always open email or answer an unknown number. WhatsApp is the channel almost everyone checks the same day.
reach.title: The message goes where people are already looking

remindersOnly.body: The automatic reminder skips those who have already replied. That's the difference between a helpful reminder and a nuisance.
remindersOnly.title: Reminders only for those who haven't replied
